findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer locations with associated routing and infrastructure. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)'. However, transformers are NOT depicted on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), Sheet 11 (Grading Plan), Sheet 19 (Wet Utilities Plan), or Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile). Although Sheet 19 and 20 include a 'Transformer Pad' symbol in their legends, no transformers are actually drawn on these sheets.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer locations must be georeferenced on all required plan sheets to facilitate utility coordination and ensure proper design integration across all disciplines. The grouping guidance specifies that 'Transformer locations must be shown consistently across multiple plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and elevation sheets)' and that 'grading and storm plans must also show transformers when those disciplines are affected by transformer placement or routing.' Omitting transformers from the wet utilities, landscape, and grading plans means these critical disciplines have not integrated the electrical infrastructure and cannot verify conflicts, clearances, or impacts.
findings.comment: Transformer locations must be shown on all required plan sheets. Currently shown only on electrical plan (Sheet 21) and site plan (Sheet 9). Missing from wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan sheets.

findings.observation: Four transformers are shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) with locations and routing identified. However, each transformer is labeled only as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no additional type designation. Vision analysis confirms: 'The transformers are solely labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". There is no information provided regarding size (e.g., kVA), specific type, or whether they are CT metered or building metered.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that drawings 'clearly delineate electrical infrastructure locations.' For Austin Energy personnel reviewing these plans, knowing whether transformers are pad-mounted, pole-mounted, vault-mounted, or service drops is critical for design coordination and construction. The generic label 'Transformer Pad' may imply pad-mounted, but explicit specification of type (using standardized designations like 'Pad-Mounted Transformer' or 'Pole-Mounted Transformer') is necessary to meet code documentation requirements.
findings.comment: Each transformer must be labeled with its type: Pad-Mounted Transformer, Pole-Mounted Transformer, Vault, or Service Drop. Current labels 'Electrical Transformer Pad' lack explicit type specification.

findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) depicts an existing transformer pad in the southeast corner of the property with a clear label 'TRANSFORMER PAD' visible in the bottom right area, along with existing overhead electric lines (OHE) and utility poles (marked TYP.). However, this existing transformer pad is NOT shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), or Sheet 11 (Grading Plan). The demolition plan (Sheet 8) notes 'Coordinate with City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines' but makes no specific reference to the existing transformer pad, and it is not marked for removal or abandonment.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, when existing electrical facilities are present on a site, their locations must be shown on all applicable plan sheets. This informs Austin Energy and other stakeholders whether the existing transformer is being retained, abandoned, replaced, or relocated. The absence of the existing transformer from the new development plans creates ambiguity about its disposition and prevents clear visual coordination of existing vs. proposed infrastructure. The grouping guidance states: 'Transformer locations must be shown consistently across multiple plan sheets' and specifies this applies 'when existing transformers present on site.'
findings.comment: Existing transformer pad shown on survey (Sheet 4) must be depicted and labeled as 'Existing' or 'EX' on all applicable plan sheets, with notation indicating whether it will be retained, removed, or replaced.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four distinct transformer pad locations distributed across the site (west of Building 1, west of Buildings 2/8, east of Building 4, and south-central between Buildings 6/7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only one transformer location labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)', positioned in the western area of the site. The single transformer shown on Sheet 9 appears to align roughly with the western area where transformers are shown on Sheet 21, but the representation is unclear. The notation '(Typ.)' on Sheet 9 suggests this is a typical or representative symbol rather than a precise location.
findings.reasoning: Transformer locations must be consistent across all plan sheets showing them so that all disciplines and reviewing agencies have a unified understanding of the infrastructure layout. When the same facilities appear on different sheets (site plan, electrical plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, grading plan), their locations should match precisely. The ambiguous representation on Sheet 9 (with a single '(Typ.)' notation) does not align clearly with the four transformers shown on Sheet 21, creating confusion about the actual number and locations of transformers on the site.
findings.comment: Transformer locations shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) must match the transformer locations shown on Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) in terms of quantity, position, and labeling. Currently, Sheet 9 shows one transformer marked '(Typ.)' while Sheet 21 shows four transformers with specific locations.

findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows tree locations throughout the site with various tree types and sizes indicated. However, no transformer pads or electrical routing is depicted on this sheet. The plan includes a legend (Key Notes) defining landscape symbols and tree abbreviations but does not show electrical infrastructure. Vision analysis confirms: 'There are no transformers explicitly shown, labeled, or depicted on this sheet... The plan does not show transformer routing, nor does it depict or verify a 10-foot lateral clearance from any transformer pads.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.10.4, no tree may be planted within 10 lateral feet of any side of pad-mounted electric equipment. The grouping guidance requires 'Plans must show transformer routing on landscape sheets to verify compliance with tree clearance requirements.' Without showing the transformer locations and their 10-foot clearance zones on the landscape plan, it is impossible to verify that tree placement complies with the code-required separation distance. This is critical information for both design review and construction oversight.
findings.comment: Transformer pad locations and 10-foot lateral clearance zones must be shown on the landscape plan to verify that tree locations comply with minimum required clearances from electrical equipment.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations as simple rectangular symbols with no clearance dimensions, clearance zones, or buffer areas indicated around them. Vision analysis confirms: 'No clearance zones marked, No indication of dedicated electrical clearance zones, specific electrical maintenance access routes, or bollard locations protecting the electrical equipment.' Transformers are shown but with no notation of required clearance distances in any direction.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies detailed clearance requirements for pad-mounted transformers including 10-ft clearance for hot-stick use areas adjacent to open areas or buildings, 15-ft clearance when facing confined spaces, 3-5 ft clearances from ventilated obstructions, 20-ft clearance from fire escapes, 5-12 ft clearance from building walls depending on material, and no covering above. These clearances must be shown on plans with dimensions and notations to document compliance. Without clearance zones depicted, review agencies cannot verify that the site design accommodates these requirements.
findings.comment: Transformer clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.4 must be clearly shown on the electrical plan with dimension lines indicating minimum clearance distances from buildings, structures, obstacles, and access areas.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric routing (blue lines) connecting service stubs to transformers and meters in plan view only. Sheet 21 references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains only water and wastewater utility profiles; no electrical profiles are provided. Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) similarly shows only water utility profiles in the 'Wtr-Ln-A' section. No profile view showing transformer locations, elevations, or proximity to existing electrical facilities (such as overhead transmission lines, underground utilities at depth, or utility conflicts) is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires 'georeferenced AutoCAD drawings that clearly delineate electrical infrastructure locations, demonstrate sufficient clearances, and show access routes.' Plan and profile exhibits showing vertical relationships (elevations, depths, clearances) are necessary to demonstrate compliance with separation distances and to identify conflicts with other utilities. Vertical profiles showing how electrical routing crosses or interfaces with storm drain, water, wastewater, and other buried infrastructure are essential for construction sequencing and conflict resolution.
findings.comment: Provide plan and profile exhibits showing transformer locations, elevations, and proximity to existing electrical facilities and other buried utilities to verify clearances and identify conflicts.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows existing overhead electric lines (OHE) running along the southern and eastern property boundaries. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) also depicts existing overhead electric lines but does not indicate distances or clearance relationships between the transformer pads and these overhead lines. No dimension lines, callouts, or notes specify the horizontal or vertical distance between any transformer pad and the nearest existing overhead line.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pad placement must account for clearances to existing overhead electrical lines per National Electrical Safety Code (NESC) standards and Austin Energy design requirements. Showing the transformer pad location without indicating its distance from existing overhead lines creates ambiguity about whether clearances are adequate. This information is essential for Austin Energy design review and for construction coordination.
findings.comment: Indicate the horizontal and vertical distance between each transformer pad and the nearest existing overhead electric line to verify compliance with required clearance distances.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Block 20 states: 'All curbing within the electric transmission easement must be laydown curbing' and 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle (5 foot spacing).' The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows transmission easement boundaries and various curb details but does not explicitly show or label curbing as 'laydown curb' in the transmission easement areas. No drivable access routes to the transformer pads are shown, and therefore no corresponding laydown curb specifications are visible. Vision analysis of Sheet 11 confirms: 'Because there are no transformers depicted or located on this specific sheet, there is no visual indication or specific spot elevations demonstrating how grading directs drainage around them.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.14.4.E, laydown curbs (which provide lower profile and allow equipment access) are required when curbing is installed within transmission easements or along Austin Energy truck access routes to transformer pads located more than 6 feet from drivable surfaces. Standard curbs impede equipment access. Sheet 3 Block 16 notes specify that grading near transmission structures must be coordinated with Austin Energy. Without showing the transformer access routes and identifying required laydown curb locations, it cannot be verified that the design accommodates Austin Energy truck access for equipment installation and maintenance.
findings.comment: Identify all curbing that falls within transmission easements or along transformer equipment pad access routes, and label as 'Laydown Curb' per UCM § 1.14.4.E and Austin Energy requirements. Show curb profiles and clearance dimensions for access.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) do not show drivable access routes to the transformer pad locations. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows transformers but does not indicate how Austin Energy trucks would access them for installation and maintenance. The grouping guidance specifies: 'Equipment pads must be located within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for Austin Energy truck accessibility unless otherwise approved by AE Design.' Without showing access routes, it cannot be verified that the transformer pads are accessible.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, pad-mounted transformers require drivable access routes for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. If a transformer is located more than 6 feet from an existing parking or traffic area, a dedicated access route must be provided and documented on the plans. Showing transformer locations without indicating access routes creates ambiguity about whether Austin Energy can reach the equipment for installation, operation, and maintenance.
findings.comment: Show drivable access routes from the nearest parking/traffic area to each transformer pad, with dimensions indicating the distance. If distance exceeds 6 feet, show the dedicated access route design.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) contains a note: 'See Sht. 19 for Profile.' However, Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) is a water/wastewater utility sheet and contains no electrical profiles. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows storm drain piping routing and details but does not overlay or cross-reference electrical routing. No profile view is provided that shows electrical conduit or cables crossing or running parallel to storm drain piping, including identification of crossing points, separation distances, or special construction details required at crossings.
findings.reasoning: When underground electrical routing crosses stormwater piping, special design considerations are required including clearance distances, use of conduit sleeves or casings at crossing points, and coordination of excavation depths. Per UCM § 1.16.0, 'georeferenced drawings' must clearly show these interactions. Without profiles showing electrical-storm drain crossings, the design cannot be reviewed for compliance with electrical and drainage standards, and the contractor cannot identify required construction sequences or protection measures.
findings.comment: Provide profile view(s) showing how underground electrical routing crosses storm drain piping, including crossing location, elevation differences, separation distance, and any special protection required at crossing points.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads as simple rectangular symbols with no indication of door locations, swing arcs, clearance zones, or operational access areas. Vision analysis confirms: 'There is no indication of door locations or designated clearance zones around the transformer pads.' The transformer pad symbols do not differentiate between different sides of the pad or indicate which side has the operating door and controls.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, the clearance requirements for pad-mounted transformers vary depending on the equipment side. Sides with operating controls/doors ('hot-stick use areas') require 10-15 ft clearance depending on whether they face open space or confined space. Sides without controls require 3-5 ft clearance. Showing the door location and control side is essential for proper site design to ensure the specified clearances are available on the correct sides of the equipment. Without this detail, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Show transformer pad door locations and control positions on the electrical plan, and indicate clearance zones appropriate to each side per UCM § 1.10.4 based on equipment orientation and adjacent features.

findings.observation: Sheet 9, 11, and 21 show various electrical easements (5' Electric & Tele. Easement, 5' P.U.E., etc.) labeled with recording information. However, these easements are shown as property-line-based boundaries and do not specifically delineate easement areas around the transformer pad locations. The grouping guidance states: 'Easement dimensions must be adequate to cover specific facility clearances and access requirements' and references UCM § 1.3.24 (Easements for Electric Distribution Facilities). No easement dimensions are verified against the specific clearance requirements for the transformer pads themselves (which require clearances ranging from 3-15 feet depending on side and use).
findings.reasoning: Austin Energy requires easements that are adequate in size to cover not only the physical location of electrical facilities but also the clearance zones and access areas required by code. The grouping notes state: 'There is no uniform "5-foot electrical easement" standard in Austin codes. Easement dimensions must be adequate to cover the physical location of facilities, required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on equipment side and configuration), and areas needed for construction, operation, maintenance, and access per UCM § 1.3.24.' Without showing transformer-specific easement boundaries with dimensions verified against code clearance requirements, compliance cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: Identify and show on plans a transformer-specific electrical easement with dimensions adequate to encompass the transformer pad location, all required clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on side), and an access zone for Austin Energy operations and maintenance.

findings.observation: Vision analysis of all plan sheets confirms no transformer screening is shown. Sheet 21 electrical plan shows transformer pads as basic symbols with no screening details. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) makes no reference to transformer screening or landscape treatment around electrical equipment. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not indicate screening. No notes, elevations, or details show whether screening walls, fencing, berms, or landscaping are planned around the transformers.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, when transformer screening is proposed to mitigate visual impact, site plans must clearly show 'Transformer screening extent, dimensions, and door swings on all plan sheets (site, grading, landscape).' This ensures that screening design does not interfere with required clearance zones or door operations, and allows Austin Energy to verify access compatibility. Screening details are also necessary for architectural and landscape integration review.
findings.comment: If transformer screening is proposed, show on site plan, landscape plan, and grading plan: screening wall/fence extent and dimensions, door swing clearances relative to screening, and landscape plantings around screening. If no screening is proposed, note 'No Screening' on electrical plan.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) labels the four transformers as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no size information. Vision analysis confirms: 'The transformers are solely labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". There is no information provided regarding size (e.g., kVA).' No kVA ratings, load specifications, or capacity information is provided for any transformer.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer documentation must include sufficient detail for Austin Energy to coordinate service adequacy with the project's electrical load. Transformer size (kVA rating) is essential information for design review, equipment ordering, and installation planning. Without size specifications, Austin Energy cannot verify that the proposed transformers are adequate to serve the project and cannot identify any shortfalls or required upgrades.
findings.comment: Each transformer must be labeled with its size in kVA (e.g., '150 kVA Pad-Mounted Transformer' or '300 kVA Pad-Mounted Transformer').

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformers as rectangular symbols with no dimension callouts indicating pad width, length, or height. Sheet 9 shows one transformer symbol as a simple rectangle with no dimensions. Pad dimensions are not provided on either sheet, making it impossible to verify consistency or to confirm that the dimensions are adequate for the specified transformer size and clearance requirements.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pad dimensions must be consistent across all plan sheets and must be adequate for the specified transformer size. Different transformer kVA ratings require different pad sizes. Per UCM § 1.10.4, pad clearance requirements depend partly on equipment size. Without documented pad dimensions, reviewing agencies cannot verify design adequacy or construction completeness.
findings.comment: Provide transformer pad dimensions (length × width × height where applicable) on all plans where transformers are shown, ensuring dimensions are consistent across sheets and adequate for the specified transformer kVA rating.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformers but provides no labeling indicating metering method. Vision analysis confirms: 'The transformers are solely labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". There is no information provided regarding... whether they are CT metered or building metered.' No notation distinguishes between CT (current transformer) metered service, standard building metered service, or other metering configurations.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer documentation must specify the metering method because this affects service design. CT metering is used for larger transformer capacities (typically above 75 kVA), while building-level metering may be used for smaller loads. The metering method impacts the location of meter installation, the service distribution enclosure configuration, and the overall electrical service design. Without this specification, coordination with Austin Energy and proper electrical design cannot be completed.
findings.comment: Label each transformer with its metering method (e.g., 'CT Metered' or 'Building Metered') to indicate how service measurement will be configured.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows eight meter locations on building exterior walls, with each labeled 'Electrical Meters.' However, meters are NOT shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) - vision analysis confirmed 'There are no electrical meters shown or labeled on this sheet.' Meters are also NOT shown on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) - vision analysis confirmed 'There are no... meters shown or labeled on this sheet.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.A, meter locations must be shown on all required plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan). This allows all reviewing disciplines to verify meter accessibility, line of sight to transformers, separation from other utilities, and landscape or site features that might interfere with meter access or visibility. Omitting meters from the site and landscape plans means these disciplines have not verified meter integration with their designs.
findings.comment: Meter locations must be shown and labeled on the site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) in addition to the electrical plan (Sheet 21).

findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) clearly shows an existing electrical meter labeled 'ELEC. METER' attached to the exterior wall of the main building structure. However, this existing meter is NOT shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), NOT shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and NOT shown on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). The demolition plan (Sheet 8) does not specifically reference the existing electrical meter, nor is it marked for removal or abandonment.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, when existing electrical facilities are present on a site, their locations must be shown on all applicable plan sheets. Similar to the existing transformer, the existing meter disposition must be clear: is it being retained, removed, or replaced? Without showing the existing meter on the development plans, there is ambiguity about its status and how it relates to the new electrical service design.
findings.comment: Show and label the existing meter (with 'EX' or 'Existing' notation) on the electrical plan, site plan, and landscape plan. Include notation indicating whether it will be abandoned, removed, or retained and integrated into the new service design.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters (one per building) on building exteriors but does not show any disconnects or service distribution enclosures. The grouping guidance states: 'When two or more meters are installed at one location and served from one set of service conductors, meters and disconnects must be grouped together in a common location with a service distribution enclosure (SDE) and wireway.' With 8 buildings and 8 individual meters, the grouping/point-of-service configuration is unclear. No legend or notes explain the service configuration.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.I and 1.9.3.4.B, when multiple meters serve a single development, they must be coordinated as a grouped metering system if they share a point of service. If each building has its own individual service point, that must be clearly documented. Without showing disconnects and grouping configuration, it cannot be determined whether the design complies with grouped metering requirements.
findings.comment: Clearly identify the service configuration: if meters are served from a single point of service, show the service distribution enclosure and disconnect locations grouped with the meters. If each building has an independent service point, note that on the plan.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows and labels eight meter locations on building exterior walls as 'Electrical Meters.' However, no disconnects are shown, labeled, or identified on the electrical plan. The grouping guidance specifies: 'Meters and disconnects must be grouped together in a common location... The disconnect must be grouped with the meter beside the AE transformer (adhering to transformer clearances per UCM § 1.10.4) or outside the building within line of sight of the transformer.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1 and 1.16.0, both meters AND disconnects must be shown and labeled on plans. The disconnect is where the customer's service is isolated from the utility service and is a critical safety component. Without showing disconnect locations, it cannot be verified that they are properly grouped with meters, within required distances, within line of sight of transformers, and accessible for emergency disconnection.
findings.comment: Show and label all service disconnects on the electrical plan. Indicate their location relative to meters (grouped together per code requirements) and verify they are within 20 feet and line of sight of the meter per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows service entry point labeled 'Underground Electric Line' at the western property boundary, transformers, pull boxes, and meters. However, no specific location is labeled as the 'Point of Service' where Austin Energy's service conductors hand off to the customer's service conductors. The grouping guidance defines point of service as 'meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or AE-approved enclosure where AE and Customer conductors connect.' While pull boxes are shown, it is unclear which component represents the actual point of service.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.3.4 and the grouping definition, the point of service must be clearly identified on plans because it defines the boundary between Austin Energy's responsibility and the customer's responsibility for electrical infrastructure. This location also determines where disconnects and service distribution enclosures must be placed per UCM § 1.9.3.1.I and 1.9.3.4.B. Without clear identification, design coordination and code compliance verification are incomplete.
findings.comment: Clearly identify and label the Point of Service (where Austin Energy service conductors connect to customer service equipment) on the electrical plan. This may be shown as a meter socket, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or other AE-approved location.

findings.observation: Sheet 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) contains two callout boxes stating 'Coordinate with City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines.' This indicates that existing utility poles and overhead electric lines are present on the site and must be coordinated for removal or relocation. However, Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show these poles with specific location callouts, nor does it provide a utility coordination drawing showing which poles are to be removed vs. retained or relocated.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, plans must show any required utility relocation. The demolition plan notes indicate pole/electric line removal is necessary but provides no visual coordination drawing. The development site plan should show existing poles, indicate which are to be removed or relocated, and show any new poles or routing required for the development. Without this coordination visible on the final site plan, contractors may not clearly understand the scope of electrical work required.
findings.comment: On the site plan (Sheet 9), clearly show existing power poles and electric lines, indicate which will be removed/relocated/retained, and show any new poles or overhead electric routing required for the development. Include Austin Energy coordination notes referencing removal approvals.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pad locations but does not indicate distances to adjacent parking or driveway areas, nor are any bollards shown. No dimensions are provided that would allow verification of whether transformer pads are within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas or outside this distance. Vision analysis confirms: 'There is no indication of dedicated electrical clearance zones, specific electrical maintenance access routes, or bollard locations protecting the electrical equipment.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, when pad-mounted transformers are located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas, 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards are required, spaced to allow equipment door opening. Bollards protect the equipment from vehicle damage. Without measuring distances from transformer pads to parking areas and showing required bollards, it cannot be verified that the site design protects equipment or meets code requirements.
findings.comment: Measure and show the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area. If any pad is within 4 feet, show bollard locations and spacing (minimum 4-inch galvanized rigid metal posts) designed to allow equipment door opening.

findings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows site contours, retaining walls, and drainage features but does not indicate transformer pad locations or spot elevations around them. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Because there are no transformers depicted or located on this specific sheet, there is no visual indication or specific spot elevations demonstrating how grading directs drainage around them.' Without transformers shown on the grading plan, it is impossible to verify that drainage slopes direct liquid flow away from buildings.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 1, grading around oil-filled pad-mounted transformer equipment must direct liquid flow away from buildings. This is a critical safety and environmental requirement. The grading plan must show transformer locations with spot elevations on all sides of the pad demonstrating that slopes direct flow away from building foundations and towards site drainage. Without this detail, code compliance cannot be verified and environmental risks cannot be assessed.
findings.comment: Show transformer pad locations on the grading plan with spot elevations on all four sides of each pad, demonstrating that ground slopes direct drainage flow away from buildings and towards site drainage areas.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters on building exteriors and four transformers at various locations, but no disconnects are shown. The code requirement per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J states: 'Maximum distance between meter and disconnect is 20 feet; they must be within line of sight of each other and readily accessible.' Without showing disconnect locations, distances between meters and disconnects cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J, the meter-to-disconnect distance is limited to a maximum of 20 feet, and they must be within line of sight of each other. This ensures that the disconnect can be located quickly in an emergency and that the electrical service can be readily shut off. Without showing disconnects on the electrical plan, this code requirement cannot be reviewed or verified during plan check or construction.
findings.comment: Show disconnect locations on the electrical plan and indicate the distance from each meter. Verify that meter-to-disconnect distance does not exceed 20 feet and that they are within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J.

findings.observation: The primary site plan set (39 sheets) does not include dedicated elevation sheets showing transformer, meter, or electrical equipment details. Sheet index in README.md lists sheets 1-39, which include site plan, utilities, grading, drainage, landscape, and construction details, but no architectural elevation sheets specific to building facades or electrical equipment elevations. Building heights are shown on Sheet 9 site plan data table, but no vertical cross-sections showing transformer locations relative to building features are provided.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer locations and clearances must be shown on elevation sheets to verify compliance with clearance requirements from windows, doors, stairs, fire escapes, and building overhangs. If the site plan set does not include elevation sheets that show transformers, this deficiency cannot be fully evaluated. It is possible that elevation sheets exist in a separate architectural drawing set not included in the primary site plan submission.
findings.comment: If transformer locations are within 20 feet of building features (windows, doors, stairs, fire escapes) per UCM § 1.10.4, transformer locations and clearances must be shown on building elevation sheets to verify compliance. Provide elevations if transformers are located adjacent to buildings.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformers serving 39 units across 8 buildings. The plan does not include a load calculation or documentation showing that four transformers are adequate to serve all buildings and units. No calculations, Austin Energy requirements letter, or specifications document is provided that confirms transformer capacity (kVA) is sufficient for the project's electrical load.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer documentation must be adequate to support Austin Energy coordination. Without documented electrical load calculations and transformer capacity specifications, it cannot be verified that the proposed transformers are adequate to serve the project. The grouping guidance states: 'Transformer quantity not adequate to serve all buildings in development' as a potential deficiency. While four transformers appear reasonable for 39 units, this must be documented with engineering calculations or Austin Energy requirements confirmation.
findings.comment: Provide electrical load calculations showing total connected load and demand for all buildings, and confirm that the proposed four transformers with specified kVA ratings are adequate to serve this load per Austin Energy requirements.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformers but does not show a switchgear, load centers, or transmission interconnects linking the transformers. The grouping guidance states: 'Switchgear location not shown when required based on electrical service configuration' and 'Requires AE Design coordination to determine applicability.' With multiple transformers (four) proposed, it is unclear whether they are configured as independent service points or as a coordinated system requiring switchgear.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, when two or more transformers are proposed, Austin Energy may require switchgear for coordination and switching capability. The necessity of switchgear is determined during Austin Energy Design coordination. Without evidence of this coordination or a documented Austin Energy requirements letter, it cannot be determined whether switchgear is required and whether its location must be shown on plans.
findings.comment: Confirm with Austin Energy Design whether switchgear is required for the four-transformer configuration. If switchgear is required, show its location and integrate it into the electrical plan with proper labeling and coordination notes.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters on building exterior walls and four transformers at various site locations. Vision analysis confirms: 'Meter locations are marked by small grouped rectangles on the building exteriors and are explicitly labeled "Electrical Meters" with leader lines pointing to them. There is no text, notation, or graphic indicating a required line of sight to the transformers.' The grouping guidance notes: 'current code requires "within sight" visibility but does not specify a maximum distance—older references to "150 ft line of sight" are not codified in current UCM.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.B, all meter locations must be 'within sight of an Austin Energy transformer.' From a 2D site plan view, it is difficult to definitively determine whether meters on building walls can see transformers located elsewhere on the site without 3D visualization or explicit line-of-sight notations. The site plan does not include sight-line annotations, distance measurements, or clear notation confirming that each meter location is within sight of at least one transformer. This creates ambiguity about compliance.
findings.comment: Indicate on the electrical plan that all meter locations are within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. Include sight-line notation or written confirmation on the plan for each meter-to-transformer relationship.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows blue lines labeled 'Underground Electric Line' routing from the service entry point (western property boundary) through pull boxes to transformers and then to meters. The routing from the primary service entry to the transformers is shown. However, the 'point of service' where customer and Austin Energy conductors connect is not clearly identified, making it ambiguous whether the service conductors 'FROM the point of service' are properly shown.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, 'Service conductors from point of service to AE facilities' must be shown. If the point of service is not clearly labeled, it is unclear which portions of the routing shown represent service conductors 'from' the point of service vs. before it. The grouping guidance defines point of service as 'meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or AE-approved enclosure where AE and Customer conductors connect,' but the electrical plan does not explicitly identify which element is the point of service.
findings.comment: Clearly identify the Point of Service location (where AE and Customer conductors connect) on the electrical plan, then verify that service conductors from this point to AE facilities (transformers, service entry) are shown and properly routed.

findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) does not indicate the presence of a moonlight tower on or within 100 feet of the property. The grouping guidance notes: 'Moonlight tower locations are not defined in code and require verification with City GIS or Austin Energy records—this cannot be determined from plans alone unless the survey shows a moonlight tower.' The property location (3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704) would need to be cross-referenced with the City of Austin moonlight tower inventory.
findings.reasoning: Per Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201, construction within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or its guy wires requires special permits, protective barriers, and enhanced insurance. However, this information is not derivable from the submitted plans and requires external verification with City GIS or Austin Energy records. The grouping guidance explicitly states this 'cannot be determined from plans alone.'
findings.comment: Verify with City of Austin GIS or Austin Energy records whether a moonlight tower exists within 100 feet of the property. If yes, show guy wire locations and labels on plans, and provide documentation of required Moonlight Tower Construction Permit.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters on building exterior walls but does not indicate proximity to gas meters, regulators, or other equipment within 3-foot separation distance. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows an existing 'GAS METER' attached to the left exterior wall of the main building structure. New site plans do not show gas meter locations or infrastructure, making it impossible to verify the 3-foot separation requirement between electrical and gas facilities.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.C, meter locations must be at least 3 feet away from gas meters, regulators, relief valves, and other electrical apparatus. Without showing both electrical meter locations and gas utility locations on the same plan, this separation requirement cannot be verified. The absence of gas utility information from the electrical plan creates ambiguity about compliance.
findings.comment: Show on the electrical plan the locations of all proposed electrical meters and reference existing/proposed gas meters, gas regulators, and other utilities to verify minimum 3-foot separation per UCM § 1.9.3.1.C.
